strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas correctness bug (GH#64643) where, on ARM, float-to-int64 overflow saturates to INT64_MAX, causing the float-to-integer “integer shortcut” to misfire and incorrectly avoid the OOB handling/exception path. The reproducing test is the added regression test for to_timedelta with a non-ns unit using value np.float64(2**63).

pinned_because: NumPy is numerically relevant but no version constraint is documented in the provided evidence, so pinning is avoided; the defect is architecture/toolchain dependent (ARM float-to-int64 overflow behavior).
Cython is required to build pandas from sources per the provided installation notes; no pin is documented.

strategy.success_criterion: The test should FAIL on the buggy revision ece14185c7f1 (no OutOfBoundsTimedelta raised due to integer-shortcut misfire) and PASS on the fixed revision from PR#64643 (OutOfBoundsTimedelta is raised with message containing "cannot convert input").
strategy.numerical_probe: value = np.float64(2**63); arr = np.array([value], dtype=np.float64); call to_timedelta(arr, unit="s")

input_output_examples.input: np.array([np.float64(2**63)], dtype=np.float64) passed as arr to to_timedelta with unit="s"
input_output_examples.buggy_output: No OutOfBoundsTimedelta raised (integer shortcut misfires due to ARM float-to-int64 saturation making (arg == arg.astype(np.int64)) evaluate True).
input_output_examples.expected_output: Raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta with match "cannot convert input"

risks: Architecture-dependent: the failure requires ARM behavior where float-to-int64 overflow saturates to INT64_MAX rather than wrapping (as described in the evidence). On x86 this test may not fail, so the transition (buggy->fixed) may not reproduce on other architectures.
Toolchain dependent: C/LLVM/ABI behavior for float-to-int64 conversion must match the ARM saturation behavior; if the platform uses different semantics, the bug may not trigger.

Versioning: the evidence provides the buggy commit hash but not the fixed commit hash; you must checkout the buggy revision and a later revision containing the in_int64_range guard logic from PR#64643 to observe the PASS transition.
Test command assumes pytest and pandas test dependencies are available after building pandas from source.

oracle.reference_source: Regression test asserts an exception type and message match: with pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta, match="cannot convert input")
oracle.why: The test does not compare numeric outputs; correctness is determined solely by whether the exception is raised on the OOB input.

fails_on_buggy.description: On ARM with buggy revision ece14185c7f1, calling to_timedelta(np.array([np.float64(2**63)], dtype=np.float64), unit="s") does not raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta because the integer-shortcut path is incorrectly taken (float-to-int64 saturation makes the all-round shortcut condition evaluate True). Thus pytest.raises fails.

passes_on_fixed.description: On ARM with the PR#64643 fix applied, the same call raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta with a message matching "cannot convert input" because the shortcut condition is guarded to exclude values outside the int64 domain (in_int64_range), forcing the vectorized OOB-handling path.
